title: CPA Order 39: Iraq's occupation-era foreign investment order and the state-enterprise sell-off that did not happen
summary: On 19 September 2003 the Coalition Provisional Authority issued Order 39. It let foreign investors own up to 100% of businesses in most sectors, but kept the ban on foreign ownership of primary extraction and initial processing of natural resources and did not apply to banks or insurers. The order did not itself sell any state enterprise. CPA plans to privatize dozens of state-owned companies were put on hold in early 2004 amid Iraqi opposition and instability. Iraq's Investment Law No. 13 of 2006 revoked Order 39, and in 2022 the government still listed 176 state-owned enterprises.

private.name: Private and foreign investors under CPA Order 39 (proposed buyers of state enterprises)
private.outcome: No wholesale transfer of state enterprises took place. In January 2004 RFE/RL reported that US officials were backing away from rapid privatization and that Bremer said such decisions must await Iraqi self-rule. In February 2004 a reported plan to privatize 150 state companies was shelved. Order 39 was revoked by Article 35 of Iraq's Investment Law No. 13 of 2006, which also excludes oil and gas extraction and production and banks and insurers. As of 2022 the government listed 176 state-owned enterprises.

claims.claim: Iraq's economy was privatized wholesale under the US occupation.
claims.explanation: Order 39 opened most sectors to foreign ownership, but it was an investment law. It did not sell anything. The CPA's announced plans to privatize state-owned companies were reported as put on hold by January-February 2004, with Bremer saying such decisions must await Iraqi self-rule. Iraq revoked Order 39 in 2006. In 2022 the Government of Iraq still listed 176 state-owned enterprises, employing an estimated 600,000 people, and a business council was still urging their privatization.

claims.claim: Order 39 handed Iraq's oil to foreign companies.
claims.explanation: Section 6(1) of Order 39 states that foreign direct and indirect ownership of the natural resources sector involving primary extraction and initial processing 'remains prohibited', and that the order does not apply to banks and insurance companies. Iraq's 2006 Investment Law likewise excludes oil and gas extraction and production. Later oil-sector contracts were a separate matter from Order 39.

claims.claim: Order 39 allowed 100% foreign ownership of Iraqi businesses.
claims.explanation: Under Section 4(2), foreign participation in new or existing business entities 'shall not be limited' unless expressly provided. Section 7 allowed wholly foreign-owned entities. The exceptions were natural-resource extraction and initial processing, banks and insurers, a deposit requirement for retail sales, and a bar on buying private real property (with use licences of up to 40 years, renewable).
